title: Tensile — Series A — v3
facts: Version 3 of the Series A deck, dated 6 July 2026
Shows June ARR of $940,000
Ask is $10M at $45M post-money — matching Aster's indicated terms
No enterprise section
body:
# Tensile — Series A

**Version 3 · 6 July 2026**

---

## 1 — The problem

Engineering teams find out their system can't handle load at the worst possible moment: in production, during an incident, with customers watching.

Existing load testing tools are used once, before a launch, by one person who knows how to drive them. Then the results go stale and nobody looks again.

---

## 2 — What we built

Tensile is continuous performance testing. Tests run in CI on every change, results are diffed against the last known good, and regressions are caught before merge rather than after deploy.

**Tensile Load** — load generation and scenario testing
**Tensile Watch** — production performance monitoring

---

## 3 — Traction

| | |
|---|---|
| ARR (June 2026) | **$940,000** |
| MRR | $78,300 |
| Growth | 11.2% average monthly, trailing six months |
| Customers | 56 |
| Net revenue retention | 118% |
| Gross margin | 80% |

Twenty-nine months from first line of code.

---

## 4 — Why retention is the number

118% net revenue retention at our ACV, in a category where most companies fight to hold 105%.

Expansion comes from two places: seat growth as more of the engineering org runs tests, and module attach as customers move from Load into Watch. Module attach is doing more of the work than we expected, which tells us the second product was the right one.

---

## 5 — Go-to-market

Self-serve generates most new logos, enterprise generates most new revenue. Enterprise deals close at 6.2x the ACV of self-serve.

Trial-to-paid conversion 6.3%, up from 4.1% after an onboarding rebuild in April.

---

## 6 — Market

Performance testing and observability tooling. We sit between the two and win when the buyer is an engineering leader who has been burned by a launch.

Primary competitors: Surge Labs, Percival. We lose most often to incumbents bundling performance into an existing observability contract, which is a pricing problem rather than a product one.

---

## 7 — Team

14 people. Ravi Menon (CEO), Dana Whitfield (CTO). Head of Engineering search in progress.

---

## 8 — The ask

**Raising $10M at $45M post-money.**

Eighteen to twenty months of runway. Funds five engineering hires, three commercial hires, and the enterprise readiness work needed to move upmarket.

---

## 9 — Use of funds

| | |
|---|---|
| Engineering | 40% |
| Go-to-market | 25% |
| Enterprise readiness | 12% |
| Infrastructure and G&A | 23% |

facts: MSA executed 30 September 2025
Initial term 12 months, expiring 30 September 2026
Annual fee $84,000, 40 named users at signature

99.5% uptime SLA with service credits

body:
# MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

**Between:** Tensile, Inc. ("Provider")
**And:** Northwind Logistics Ltd. ("Customer")
**Effective Date:** 30 September 2025

---

## 1. Definitions

**"Service"** means the Tensile load testing and performance monitoring platform as described in the applicable Order Form.

**"Named User"** means an individual authorised by Customer to access the Service under Customer's account.

**"Order Form"** means an ordering document executed by both parties referencing this Agreement.

---

## 2. Term

**2.1 Initial Term.** This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for twelve (12) months, expiring **30 September 2026** (the "Initial Term").

**2.2 Renewal.** This Agreement does not renew automatically. Any continuation beyond the Initial Term requires a new Order Form executed by both parties prior to expiry.

**2.3 Termination for cause.** Either party may terminate on thirty (30) days written notice of a material breach that remains uncured.

---

## 3. Fees

**3.1** Annual fee for the Initial Term: **$84,000 USD**, invoiced annually in advance.

**3.2** The fee covers up to forty (40) Named Users. Usage above that threshold is billed quarterly in arrears at $150 per additional Named User per month.

**3.3** Payment terms net thirty (30) days from invoice date.

---

## 4. Service Levels

**4.1 Availability.** Provider will maintain 99.5% monthly uptime, excluding scheduled maintenance notified at least seventy-two (72) hours in advance.

**4.2 Service credits.** Where monthly availability falls below the commitment:

| Monthly availability | Credit |
|---|---|
| 99.0% – 99.5% | 5% of monthly fee |
| 95.0% – 99.0% | 10% of monthly fee |
| Below 95.0% | 25% of monthly fee |

**4.3 Support.** Business hours support, 09:00–18:00 UK time, weekdays. Sev-1 response within four (4) hours.

---

## 5. Data Protection and Security

**5.1** Provider shall process Customer Data solely to provide the Service.

**5.2** Provider shall maintain industry-standard technical and organisational measures, including encryption at rest and in transit.

**5.3** Provider shall notify Customer of any personal data breach within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware.

**5.4** Sub-processors are listed at tensile.dev/subprocessors. Provider will give thirty (30) days notice of additions.

**5.5** Customer Data is hosted in the eu-west-2 region.

---

## 6. Access and Authentication

**6.1** Customer is responsible for managing its Named Users and for the security of their credentials.

**6.2** Provider requires multi-factor authentication on all accounts.

---

## 7. Limitation of Liability

**7.1** Neither party's aggregate liability shall exceed the fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim.

**7.2** Neither party is liable for indirect or consequential loss.

---

## 8. General

**8.1** Governing law: England and Wales.

**8.2** This Agreement, together with any Order Form, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties and supersedes all prior representations, whether oral or written.

**8.3** No variation is effective unless in writing and signed by both parties.

---

**EXECUTED 30 September 2025**

For Tensile, Inc. — Ravi Menon, Chief Executive Officer
For Northwind Logistics Ltd. — Linda Marsh, VP Engineering

# Tensile — Q2 2026 Board Meeting

**18 June 2026** · Prepared by Ravi Menon
Attending: Ravi Menon, Dana Whitfield, Nadia Osei

---

## 1. Headline

| | May 2026 | Change vs Feb 2026 |
|---|---|---|
| ARR | $860,000 | +39% |
| MRR | $71,700 | |
| Customers | 52 | +14 |
| Net revenue retention | 118% | +4pts |
| Net burn | $175,000 / mo | +$20k |
| Cash | $1.90M | |
| Runway | 11 months | −4 months |
| Headcount | 13 | +2 |

---

## 2. Financial detail

Burn up $20,000 per month since February, driven by the two hires and the compensation band adjustment made in May. Infrastructure cost reduction delivered as planned — our own workloads are down roughly 45% and gross margin recovered to 80%.

Runway is 11 months. This is the number that sets the timeline for everything else in this document.

---

## 3. Series A — approval requested

**Requesting formal approval to raise $12M.**

At planned burn, $12M funds approximately 24 months. That period covers:

| Use | Amount | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Engineering — 5 hires incl. Head of Engineering | ~$4.4M | Enterprise build and delivery capacity |
| Go-to-market — 3 hires | ~$2.6M | Enterprise motion requires people who have run one |
| Enterprise readiness — SOC 2, identity, residency | ~$1.2M | Currently a revenue blocker, see section 5 |
| Infrastructure and G&A | ~$2.4M | |
| Buffer | ~$1.4M | |

The alternative — raising $8M — funds 16 months and forces the enterprise build to be sequenced rather than parallel. We think that's a false economy given section 5.

Process: materials ready, first conversations begin late June, target term sheet by mid-August.

---

## 4. Product

**Shipped in Q2:** onboarding simplification (trial-to-paid 4.1% → 6.3%), infrastructure cost reduction, tracing private beta to eight accounts.

**Deferred out of Q2:** tracing GA moved to Q3 on two blocking issues in the sampling path. Billing revamp sequenced behind it.

**Q3 plan:** tracing GA mid-August, onboarding v2, billing revamp, audit log export.

---

## 5. Enterprise readiness — commercial risk

New item on this agenda, raised deliberately.

Two deals stalled in security review this quarter — one on federated identity, one on EU data residency. Neither capability is currently scheduled.

Quantifying the exposure. Accounts with an identity or compliance requirement we cannot presently meet, measured as ARR at renewal risk over the next twelve months:

| Account | ARR | Requirement | Renewal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Northwind Logistics | $84,000 | SAML SSO, audit log export | 30 Sep 2026 |
| Calder Systems | $62,000 | SOC 2 Type II report | 1 Jan 2027 |
| Bastion Freight | $48,000 | SOC 2 Type II report | 1 Mar 2027 |
| **Total** | **$190,000** | | |

That is 22% of current ARR.

Audit log export is scoped for Q3. SOC 2 observation begins October. **Federated identity is not scheduled in Q3** — the quarter is consumed by tracing GA and the billing revamp, and identity is a five-to-seven week build with an auth-path migration we are unwilling to run alongside a GA.

Current plan places identity in Q4, October to November.

The board should understand that this sequencing accepts risk on the Northwind renewal specifically, as it is the only one of the three that falls due before the capability lands.

---

## 6. Head of Engineering

Search opened in May. Approved band $240,000 base, up to 0.8% equity — set at roughly the 60th percentile after losing two candidates on compensation earlier in the year.

Four candidates in process, two at final stage. Target start date 1 October.

---

## 7. Q3 preview

Objectives: close the Series A, reach $1.3M ARR, ship audit log export and tracing GA, fill the Head of Engineering role.

Next meeting 17 September 2026.

## Commercial

| Account Executive (OTE) | $136,000 | $150,000 | $176,000 | $150,000 |
| Head of Sales | $125,000 | $145,000 | $168,000 | $145,000 |
| Support Engineer | $50,000 | $58,000 | $68,000 | $55,000–$65,000 |

## Equity guidance

| Level | Range |
|---|---|
| Software Engineer | 0.05% – 0.12% |
| Senior Engineer | 0.12% – 0.25% |
| Staff / EM | 0.25% – 0.45% |
| Head of function | 0.5% – 0.8% |

## Conclusion

We were sitting near the 40th percentile across engineering, which explains
two offer declines in Q1 and roughly six weeks lost per attempt.

**Recommendation, adopted May 2026:** move all engineering bands to the 60th
percentile. Cost impact roughly $34,000 annually across current headcount,
against a hiring delay cost we estimated as considerably higher.

Anything above band requires board approval before an offer is issued.

# Tensile — Q1 2026 Board Meeting

**12 March 2026** · Prepared by Ravi Menon
Attending: Ravi Menon, Dana Whitfield, Nadia Osei

---

## 1. Headline

| | February 2026 | Change vs Nov 2025 |
|---|---|---|
| ARR | $620,000 | +38% |
| MRR | $51,700 | |
| Customers | 38 | +9 |
| Net revenue retention | 114% | +3pts |
| Net burn | $155,000 / mo | +$14k |
| Cash | $2.40M | |
| Runway | 15 months | |
| Headcount | 11 | +2 |

Three consecutive months above 10% MRR growth. Retention is the number we're proudest of.

---

## 2. Financial detail

Burn increased $14,000 per month over the quarter, split roughly evenly between two engineering hires and infrastructure. Infrastructure is running hotter than modelled — our own load-generation workloads are now a material line item, which is a good problem to have discovered before a customer did.

Gross margin 78%, down two points, same cause.

We remain on plan for the FY26 budget approved in November.

---

## 3. Product

**Shipped this quarter:** results diffing in CI, scheduled test runs, three integrations.

**In progress:** distributed tracing, private beta targeted for April.

Tracing is the largest bet we're making this year. It moves us from "the tool you use before a release" to "the tool that's on during the incident," and it's the difference between a $20k account and a $80k one.

---

## 4. Go-to-market

Self-serve continues to generate the majority of new logos and a minority of new revenue. Enterprise deals close at 6.2x the ACV of self-serve, with a sales cycle of 71 days against 4.

Trial-to-paid conversion is 4.1% and has been flat since October. We believe onboarding friction is the cause and are testing a simplified first-run in April.

**Lost deals this quarter:** three. Two to incumbents bundling into existing observability contracts, one on price.

---

## 5. Team

Eleven people. Two engineering hires closed in Q1.

Dana is currently the only engineering manager, with six direct reports. This is workable now and won't be by mid-year.

---

## 6. Discussion — Series A timing

Current plan has us raising in Q4 2026 with roughly nine months of runway remaining at the point of starting.

**Recommendation from Nadia, for discussion:** begin groundwork in Q2 instead. Build the materials, start the relationships, and be in a position to run a process from a position of choice rather than need.

The counter-argument is distraction. A raise costs the CEO roughly half of three months.

**Resolution:** agreed to start Q2 groundwork. Formal approval to raise deferred to the Q2 meeting.

---

## 7. Asks of the board

1. Introductions to funds that lead infrastructure rounds at Series A
2. SOC 2 auditor recommendations
3. Head of Engineering candidates — role not yet opened, but sourcing informally

title: Northwind Vendor Security Questionnaire — Completed
body:
# Vendor Security Questionnaire — Tensile, Inc.

**Completed by:** Dana Whitfield, CTO
**Returned:** 26 May 2026
**Requested by:** Karin Holt, Information Security, Northwind Logistics

---

## Section 1 — Encryption

**1.1 Data at rest?** AES-256. AWS EBS and S3 with SSE-KMS.

**1.2 Data in transit?** TLS 1.3 minimum. TLS 1.2 rejected at the load balancer.

**1.3 Key management?** AWS KMS, customer-managed keys not currently offered. Annual rotation.

---

## Section 2 — Infrastructure

**2.1 Hosting?** AWS, eu-west-2 (London).

**2.2 Multi-tenancy?** Logical isolation with row-level tenant scoping. No physical isolation offered.

**2.3 Backups?** Daily, thirty-five day retention, quarterly restore testing.

---

## Section 3 — Incident response

**3.1 Documented process?** Yes.

**3.2 Notification commitment?** 24 hours from becoming aware of a personal data breach.

**3.3 Incidents in last 12 months?** One Sev-1, 14 February 2026, 47 minutes, capacity exhaustion in the load generator fleet. No data exposure. Affected customers notified same day.

---

## Section 4 — Subprocessors

AWS (hosting), Stripe (payments), Postmark (transactional email), Sentry (error tracking). Published list maintained, thirty days notice of additions.

---

## Section 5 — Personnel

**5.1 Background checks?** Yes, for all employees with production access.

**5.2 Security training?** Annual, mandatory.

**5.3 Offboarding?** Access revoked within 4 hours of departure.

---

## Section 6 — Business continuity

RTO 4 hours, RPO 1 hour. Tested quarterly.

---

## Section 7 — Access control ⚠️

**7.1 Federated identity (SAML/OIDC)?** **Not supported.** All users authenticate directly against Tensile.

**7.2 MFA?** Enforced on all accounts. TOTP and WebAuthn.

**7.3 Role-based access control?** Partial. Two roles — admin and member. Granular permissions not available.

**7.4 SCIM provisioning?** Not supported.

---

## Section 8 — Vulnerability management

**8.1 Penetration testing?** Annual, third party. Last conducted November 2025, no critical or high findings outstanding.

**8.2 Dependency scanning?** Automated, on every build.

---

## Section 9 — Audit and logging ⚠️

**9.1 Access events logged?** Yes.

**9.2 Retention?** Ninety days, internal only.

**9.3 Customer-accessible export?** **Not available.**

**9.4 Configurable retention?** Not available.

---

## Section 10 — Certifications

**10.1 SOC 2?** No report. Type II observation window begins October 2026. Report expected mid-2027.

**10.2 ISO 27001?** No.

**10.3 GDPR?** Yes — DPA available, data hosted in EU, sub-processor list published.

---

*Answers provided in good faith. Sections 7 and 9 identify known gaps; we would rather disclose them than have them discovered.*
